excerpt.text: From the ledgers of Iris Penhale, dressmaker, Walcot Street, Bath

excerpt: 12 May 1998. Lyall: the Eleanor dress (1956, ivory silk faille). Bride, Miss A. Corrigan.

excerpt.text: Take in waist 1.5 cm. New hooks and eyes. Hem to her shoes, not the floor. Laughs a lot. Wants pockets. No.

excerpt: She thought about the words, which she could see without the calico in front of her; she would be able to see them for some time.

excerpt.text: He’s done it again. Not he will. Not be careful.
As if whoever wrote it had been sure that the next woman to read it would already be too late.

caption:
12 May 1998. A dressmaker’s ledger: ‘Laughs a lot. Wants pockets. No.’

One month later: ‘She looked happy.’

Twenty-eight years on, the same dress comes back up the stairs.
